author: reek
body: Adversarial probe (ProofTotalityProbe Stage 2, positive proof-term grammar). The body of a proof-typed definition is an inline if-expression, not a proof term. There is NO name cycle, so Stage 1's acyclicity check (CDX4023) passes it; the positive grammar (CDX4024) rejects the disallowed form. The proposition here is true, so the point is the FORM: an if-expression is not part of the proof calculus, and admitting one would let an if launder a proof of a false proposition (the false-proposition version needs 'assume' in a branch, which adds a CDX4021 warning; this probe keeps a single code). The sound recursion a proof needs is 'induction'; the honest escape hatch is 'assume'.
